<reason>B won a competitive debate by making “enough” the live decision rule and showing A never met it. A’s strongest live route was that mixed universal tools cannot restore trips women categorically refuse, and a timeout only returns them to the old baseline. B conceded the pairing point, then used thin night supply, always-on platform costs, and A’s own “any rate above zero” threshold to show occasional arrivals do not justify the complexity. A’s weakly-dominant lottery was sharp, but it declined the weighing the motion requires.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2: accepting that PIN-matched mixed rides do not restore categorical refusal, then collapsing A’s “any rate above zero” into a failed sufficiency standard against always-on costs.</best_rebuttal>
